We are the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.
We're training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.
We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.
We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!
 The role 
You'll lead marketing operations and analytics at Cohere. That covers the team, the martech stack, how we measure marketing's contribution to pipeline, and the budget and pipeline numbers marketing plans against. When leadership asks what marketing produced last quarter and what to fund next, the answer starts with your numbers.
The role reports to the VP of Brand. You'll work most closely with the Marketing Chief of Staff and the heads of Growth and Demand and Product Marketing, and every week with Revenue Operations, Sales Operations & Finance. Web operations is part of marketing but doesn't report to this role.
 The team 
You'll manage the marketing operations, automation, and analytics and data operations staff, and hire where you find gaps. Marketing is growing rapidly, so you'll also bring acquired companies' systems and data into our stack.
 Measurement 
The attribution methodology is yours, documented and signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance. Each quarter you'll present marketing's pipeline contribution to the executive team and say what you'd change. Your analysts do the same for the program teams in Growth and Demand, Events and Product Marketing, showing which campaigns and channels are paying back their spend.
 Systems and data 
Marketo, Looker, GA4 and 6sense are yours end-to-end, along with the campaign and lead side of Salesforce. That includes forms, nurture, lead lifecycle, scoring and routing. Campaign data needs to be structured well enough that analysts don't need workarounds, and target-account data has to reconcile to the governed account list. With Revenue Operations, you'll make sure the data behind marketing's pipeline numbers can't change without a record, so a bulk edit can't quietly rewrite marketing's results. A/B testing on nurture and forms sits with you too, sized so the results can be read.
Over time we want fewer tools and fewer dashboards, with one governed source for each metric.
 Budget and planning numbers 
You'll own the martech and operations budget and track budget and headcount across marketing. You'll also build the pipeline and capacity models marketing plans against. The Marketing Chief of Staff runs planning and the business reviews and leads the trade-off conversations with your numbers in hand. Marketing and Sales need to count pipeline the same way, every time.
 Your first year 
In the first 90 days, you'll document the attribution methodology and get it signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance. By then we should also have an inventory of every reporting surface, each with a named owner, and your order for fixing the data problems you inherit.

GTM Architect at Workleap - AI & RevOps Career Growth in Wilmington
This is a genuinely rare role sitting at the intersection of AI engineering, revenue operations, and go-to-market strategy — a trifecta that is commanding increasing market premiums in 2024–2025. "GTM Architect" or "GTM Engineer" titles are emerging as some of the fastest-growing roles in B2B SaaS, and early movers building this skillset are well-positioned.
 Compensation context: The base range of CAD $110k–$140k (OTE up to $155k) is competitive for a senior IC role at a Canadian tech company, though it trails comparable US-based roles by 20–30%. The LTIP is a meaningful differentiator for a ~20-year-old profitable company.
Agentic AI workflow design using LLMs, MCP connectors, and tools like n8n — highly transferable and in short supply.
Signal-based GTM strategy (product-led growth meets AI-driven outbound) — a rapidly maturing discipline.
SQL-backed revenue analytics tied directly to business outcomes (renewals, NRR, LTV).
Cross-functional stakeholder management without a PM — high autonomy, high visibility.
 Green flags: No bureaucratic PM layer, clear ownership of business metrics, and a company with 15,000+ paying customers providing real production data to work with. The take-home case study hiring process signals they want proven builders, not credential collectors.
 Watch for: "We move fast" and "ambiguity doesn't slow you down" language suggests a high-intensity environment. This suits senior ICs but may be challenging if you prefer structured roadmaps.
Company Description
Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart — we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent , our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate , the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.
Your Role
ShareGate's customers generate rich signals (product usage, support interactions, renewal dates), but those signals aren't yet connected into an engine that protects and grows the revenue we already have. As our GTM Architect, Expansion & Retention, you'll design, build and ship AI agents and agentic workflows that turn those signals into saved renewals and cross-sell pipeline. This is an embedded engineering role within GTM, not back-office ops: you'll apply the signal-based, agent-first approach we already use for new customer acquisition to the customers we already have.
 Your impact: 
Protect renewals by building AI agents that continuously monitor renewal health and flag at‑risk accounts to Account Managers early, with context, recommended next steps and enough lead time to act.
Grow revenue from existing customers by designing and running an agentic cross‑sell motion: score fit for our second product line, research each account, personalize outreach, qualify interest and route genuine intent to the right salesperson with the full context needed to close.
Define the signals your agents need and partner with Revenue Systems, which builds and owns the data flow between product usage and the CRM. Validate the data with SQL before you act on it.
Replace manual workflows with AI agents and reusable pipeline modules (not one-off automations) that Account Management and Sales can run and own on their own.

The Opportunity: 
We are looking for a delivery-focused Project Manager to run acquisition migrations end-to-end as Beacon standardizes each newly acquired company onto a common GTM stack. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who runs several projects at once against a hard deadline, keeps a lot of moving parts coordinated, and raises the bar on the quality of work around them.
Beacon acquires roughly one software company per week which is then integrated into our standardized GTM stack. This role partners with newly acquired companies starting from the first discovery call, through CRM and Support Ticketing builds, until systems are fully rolled out. This role coordinates internal resources and ensures the portfolio company is trained on the tech stack while adhering to an SLA and making the process more repeatable with every acquisition.
This role is responsible for running the project, meaning holding the timeline, managing the stakeholders, directing the build resources, and making sure what ships is right. This role will be partnered with a technical RevOps resource to help with deeper technical support, but this role will be responsible for speaking to the toolset at a high-level.
 What You Would Own: 
 Migration delivery. Acquisition migrations against our SLA, owned end to end: scoping, project planning, sequencing the CRM and Support Ticketing builds, coordinating data migration, and making sure the team is trained and confident at go-live. You would lead discovery calls to assess their current stack and map it to Beacon's standards, hold the plan and the timeline across several concurrent migrations, manage dependencies and risks before they become slips, and own the status.
 Contractor direction and quality. You would direct the work of pooled implementation contractors assigned to your migrations, pull in technical support when a problem genuinely needs it, make day-to-day scope and sequencing calls within the documented playbook, and escalate only genuine exceptions.
 Delivery process. Improving the migration playbook as you run against it — tightening the plan, the checklists, and the handoffs so each acquisition goes faster and more predictably than the last.
 Who You Are: 
 You have 3–5 years project or program management, running implementation, migration or change management projects — ideally in B2B SaaS, professional services, or consulting. You ideally have managed multiple projects concurrently against firm deadlines..
 You are literate in Go-To-Market systems. You understand how a CRM and a support platform are put together and can scope a build, and hold a credible conversation with a founder about their GTM tech stack.
 You have directed the work of others — contractors, an agency pod, or junior admins — even without formal people management.
 A confident stakeholder-facing communicator. You’re a people person who can understand hesitant stakeholders and help them feel excited during a period of a lot of change.
 Strong judgment under ambiguity. You make defensible calls from a playbook instead of escalating everything, and you know which exceptions genuinely warrant escalation.
 A quality bar you set rather than inherit. You care how the build looks six months after go-live, not just at handoff.
 Strong written communication. Much of this job is a clear status update landing in the right inbox at the right time
 A bias for action. You would rather move something forward than perfect the plan
 The agility to adapt when a program changes shape mid-stream, and the confidence to get hands-on when it needs you
 Nice to Have: 
Formal project management training or certification (PMP or similar).
Familiar with project management tools (Asana, JIRA, Monday.com).
Hands-on CRM experience (HubSpot, Salesforce, PipeDrive, Zoho, etc.)
Hands-on Support experience (Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, etc.)
M&A exposure, particularly post-close systems consolidation.
Familiarity with migration tooling or scripting that moves data faster and more reliably than manual imports allow.
 Our Values at Beacon Software 
Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.

az-ca-5961946485.description:
Escalon is a Toronto-based AI consultancy built by engineers. We help enterprises redesign their workflows around AI, then engineer, test and run those systems in production.
Our roots are in high-performance software, quality engineering and program delivery across gaming, SaaS and enterprise systems. That discipline is what makes AI hold up in the real world.
About the role
As a GTM Engineer you build the systems behind Escalon's growth: automated prospecting, lead enrichment and outreach workflows that put the right conversations in front of our team.
We are looking for a GTM operator who is also a hands-on builder. You understand how a revenue team works, you can turn its problems into working automations, and you have built those solutions yourself rather than only managing the tools and processes around them.
Our buyer and prospect signals live across a CRM, enrichment tools, outreach platforms, and public and third-party data. You will connect those sources, add context, and build workflows that show our team who to engage, why, when and with what message.
You do not need to be a traditional software engineer. You may come from revenue operations, sales operations, marketing operations, GTM systems or a similar technical GTM function. Because Escalon builds AI systems for clients, you will also be a first-hand user of the kind of AI workflows we recommend.
Clay CRM and workflow automation Lead enrichment Outreach tooling Data and integrations
What you'll do
Build prospecting and enrichment workflows: design and run automated account research, lead enrichment, scoring and prioritization that keep our pipeline full of the right companies and contacts.
Turn signals into action: connect and enrich data from the CRM, outreach tools, web activity and third-party sources to identify high-value accounts and recommend the next step.
Automate the GTM stack: build integrations and workflows across the CRM, Clay, sales engagement and outreach tools, enrichment providers and internal data sources.
Build agents and internal tools: use LLMs, APIs, webhooks, automation platforms and scripting to create tools that make our team faster and more effective.
Design outreach workflows: set up sequencing, personalization and follow-up, and keep them accurate, compliant with email and privacy rules, and well measured.
Prototype and iterate quickly: get solutions into users' hands, measure what works, and improve them from real feedback.
Make workflows reliable: add validation, guardrails, human review where it matters, monitoring and error handling so automations can be trusted in production.
Keep data clean: own data quality across tools so records, owners and statuses stay consistent as volume grows.
What you need
Experience in revenue operations, sales operations, GTM systems, marketing operations or a similar GTM function.
A solid understanding of B2B revenue workflows: lead management, routing, enrichment, qualification, account prioritization, prospecting and pipeline generation.
Hands-on experience building automations, integrations, internal tools or data workflows yourself.
Experience with GTM platforms such as Clay, a CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce or similar), and outreach or sales engagement tools.
Experience building AI or LLM-powered workflows, with tools such as Claude, OpenAI, n8n, Zapier, Make or similar.
Comfort working with APIs, webhooks and scripting to connect systems.
The ability to work directly with the people who use your systems and translate their problems into working solutions.
Nice to have
Experience building account intelligence, scoring, routing or signal-based GTM workflows.
Experience taking an automation or AI workflow from prototype through production and adoption.
Experience in a consulting, services or other B2B environment with long sales cycles.
Escalon is committed to an inclusive hiring process and to equal opportunity. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and consider every applicant on their skills and experience. If you need an accommodation at any stage of the process, let us know and we will work with you.

Responsable du marketing produit
 About AppDirect 
Become a digital, global citizen and enable the new generation of digital entrepreneurs around the world. AppDirect offers a subscription commerce platform to sell any product, through any channel, on any device - as a service. We power millions of subscriptions worldwide for organizations. We do this by our values-driven culture—one that enables you to Be Seen, Be Yourself, and Do Your Best Work.
 About You 
You are a product marketer who has moved beyond execution and is ready to own a product line end to end. For this role, you will be the sole product marketing voice for the Business Unit. You need to be comfortable setting your own priorities and driving work forward without day-to-day direction. You translate competitive intelligence, win/loss data, and customer insight into clear positioning and concrete go-to-market plans that sales and product teams can act on. You understand how analyst relations work and you know how to work with customers to build advocacy and expansion-stage marketing programs. You are equally at home writing a sharp positioning narrative and reviewing pipeline data to assess whether your launches are working. Working alongside two other product marketing managers and a director of product management, you contribute the Business Unit perspective to cross-functional planning discussions and make sure sales, customer success, and marketing leaders feel aligned on priorities.
 What you'll do and how you'll have an impact 
Own the full go-to-market strategy for Business Unit’s Product launches, including positioning, success criteria, and cross-functional execution.
Define product marketing outcomes and success metrics tied to the Business Unit pipeline and new revenue targets, and track performance against them.
Partner directly with the Director of Product Management to shape the product roadmap using competitive intelligence, win/loss analysis, and market research.
Build and execute Business Unit's customer marketing strategy, with a focus on advocacy programs and expansion-stage motions that support cross-sell across AppDirect's unified monetization platform.
Own analyst relations for the Business Unit, including briefings, inquiries, and ongoing positioning with research firms such as Gartner.
Represent the product marketing perspective in cross-functional planning discussions with sales, customer success, and marketing leadership, translating business priorities into a clear product marketing roadmap.
Contribute to pricing analysis and provide recommendations to inform Business Unit's packaging and positioning decisions.
 What we're looking for 
3–5 years of product marketing experience in a B2B SaaS environment, with demonstrated ownership of go-to-market strategy.
Experience conducting competitive analysis, win/loss research, or market intelligence and using those findings to influence product or positioning decisions.
Familiarity with analyst relations processes, including preparing briefings and responding to research inquiries.
Experience developing customer marketing or expansion-stage programs (advocacy, upsell, or cross-sell campaigns).
Ability to work autonomously across multiple initiatives—this matters because you will be the primary product marketing owner for a Business Units and will set your own agenda without close oversight.
Clear, structured communication skills across written and verbal formats—this matters because you will regularly present positioning and strategy to sales leadership, product management, and executive stakeholders.
Experience with product-led growth (PLG) strategies is an asset, not a requirement.
At AppDirect, we believe that innovation thrives in an environment that houses diversity of excellence, experience and thought. We respect each AppDirector as their own fingerprint; unique with no one alike. We foster an environment of inclusion without regard to race, religion, age, sexual orientation, or gender identity enabling AppDirectors to embrace their uniqueness to do their best work. As such, we strongly encourage applications from Indigenous peoples, racialized people, people with disabilities, people from gender and sexually diverse communities, and/or people with intersectional identities.
At AppDirect we take privacy very seriously. For more information about our use and handling of personal data from job applicants, please read our Candidate Privacy Policy. For more information of our general privacy practices, please see AppDirect Privacy Notice: https://www.appdirect.com/about/privacy-notice

AI tools do not make hiring decisions or solely automated decisions about your candidacy – all decisions are made by our people. (On-site - reports to the VP, Sales)
About Clutch
We’re on a mission to reinvent the way people buy, sell, and own cars.
Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car buying and selling experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse hundreds of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee... and that’s just the beginning.
Named two years in a row to the Globe & Mail’s list of the Top Growing Companies in Canada and also awarded spots on Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50TM and Fast 500TM lists, we’re looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team.
Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017 and currently services Ontario, British Columbia, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is backed by a number of world-class investors, including D1 Capital, Altos Ventures, BMO Capital Partners, Canaan, Real Ventures, and others. To learn more, visit clutch.ca.
About the role
We’re looking for a smart, resourceful, and analytically strong individual to join our Revenue team as Strategy and Operations Manager (Revenue). This role is an exceptional opportunity for someone early in their career 1-5 years post-grad who’s hungry to drive impact across a high-growth sales organization - working side by side with our VP of Sales on strategic initiatives, performance insights, and cross-functional projects that unlock growth.
What You’ll Do
Project-Based Execution
Lead and execute small to medium-sized strategic projects that drive incremental improvement across the sales team—ranging from process optimization to frontline tools to performance analysis.
Take ownership of project scoping, planning, execution, and results measurement—working across disciplines to see initiatives through end-to-end.
Ruthlessly prioritize initiatives that move the needle and align with broader revenue goals.
Work Cross-Functionally to Drive Change
Collaborate with Sales, Product, Marketing, Customer Experience, and Engineering to remove friction in the sales process and bring structure to ambiguity.
Be equally comfortable building a business case in Excel, presenting findings to the VP Sales, or jumping into a call with a distressed customer to understand root causes.
Translate complex problems into actionable insights—and ensure action happens.
Data-Driven Insights & Sales Strategy
Dive deep into sales and funnel data to uncover insights and opportunities. You’ll be expected to bring a strong analytical toolkit and be an 8+/10 when it comes to working with data.
Support forecasting, territory planning, performance dashboards, and root cause analysis to inform sales leadership decision-making.
Develop simple, clear, and persuasive recommendations backed by data and common sense.
Self-Learning & Experimentation
Take initiative to self-learn new tools, frameworks, and strategies—whether it’s mastering ChatGPT, learning how to write SQL, or figuring out how a new system works with minimal handholding.
Be proactive in experimenting with new ideas, rapidly testing assumptions, and applying learnings in real-time.
Develop comfort navigating ambiguity and unfamiliar territory—you’ll regularly tackle challenges that don’t come with a playbook.
What We’re Looking For
1-5 years of experience in management consulting, investment banking, sales strategy, business operations, or a high-performing startup environment.
8+/10 with data: Strong proficiency with Excel/Sheets required; experience with SQL, BI tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau)
Proven ability to lead structured projects and think strategically, while also rolling up your sleeves to get things done.
Comfortable with ambiguity and change—able to thrive in a fast-paced, ever-evolving environment.
Intellectually curious, fast learner, and someone who brings strong judgment and common sense to every conversation.
Strong communication and collaboration skills—you’re just as comfortable with execs as you are with frontline staff or developers.
Gritty, humble, and high-agency: you take initiative, own problems, and don’t wait to be told what to do.
Nice to Have
A genuine interest in Clutch’s industry—automotive, marketplaces, consumer tech, or the future of retail.
Passion for building things from the ground up and a desire to grow into a leadership role in the future.
Why Clutch
Partner directly with the VP Sales on initiatives that materially impact top-line performance.
Solve meaningful problems, fast: You’ll be in the room where decisions happen and have the chance to influence direction across the business.
Build your career: Whether your goal is GM, Product, Strategy, or Ops—this role sets a strong foundation for growth.
Competitive package: Market cash, equity upside, full benefits, and a collaborative in-office culture built on pace and curiosity.
Employment Type:
Existing, Permanent Full-Time
Compensation & Benefits:
Salary range: $110k - $130k (plus equity)
Benefits: Comprehensive benefits plans include healthcare, dental care, vision care, prescriptions, life insurance and dependent coverage; start from day 1. (Applicable for Permanent Full-Time)
Pay decisions reflect objective criteria: skills, performance, market benchmarking, responsibilities and working conditions.
Clutch is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where all individuals have an opportunity to succeed. If you require accommodation at any stage of the interview process, please email talent@clutch.ca.

The role will have a strong focus on customer pricing, profitability, category insights, financial modeling, forecasting, inventory optimization and P&L performance. Serve as the financial business partner to the Foodservice Sales and Marketing leadership team.

Build pricing and profitability models incorporating product cost, freight, duties, currency, inventory, working capital, rebates, billbacks and other customer-specific costs.

Partner with Sales and Marketing to assess volume, pricing and margin scenarios before commercial commitments are made.
Develop dashboards and reporting metrics on customer, product, category and sales performance.
Analyze customer and product profitability and identify opportunities to improve gross margin and contribution.
Analyze price, volume and mix changes and their impact on Foodservice profitability.
Analyze sales trends, seasonality, and customer patterns to improve demand forecasts.
Review volume trends to plan and identify root causes of forecast variances.
Develop reporting on forecast performance at customer, category, SKU and regional levels.
Identify trends early to prevent shortages or excess inventory.

Monitor inbound container activity, truckload and import schedules to optimize inventory placement.
Review transfer activity between warehouses and identify opportunities to improve efficiency.
Recommend product allocation strategies that minimize transfers, freight expense and out-of-stock issues.
Monitor safety stock requirements and recommend adjustments based on demand patterns.
Other duties as assigned.

Sr. Analyst, Global Incentive Compensation
 Position Description 
The Global Incentive Compensation (GIC) team at Salesforce is a global leader for sales compensation in the technology industry. We manage the sales compensation for all Salesforce, end-to-end - from designing the sales compensation plan to enable the company’s go-to-market strategy to administering the payment so that our sales teams get paid on time. Within GIC, the Data Strategy team owns the foundational data architecture, data modeling, and secure data-sharing pipelines that power our global operational ecosystem (supporting $3B+ in annual commissions). We are hiring a Senior Technical Data Analyst to act as a key hands-on developer and business translator. This is a highly visible, active role. We are looking for an analyst who goes beyond simply executing transactional queries to designing and transforming data in our Snowflake Gold and Reporting database layers. You will serve as the ultimate operational bridge: partnering deeply with upstream business teams (Decision Analytics and Reporting) to run technical discovery, clarify business requirements, and then rolling up your sleeves to write production-grade SQL code to deliver clean, curated, and highly aggregated datasets to support complex reporting and high-priority, time sensitive ad-hoc business needs. Crucially, you are a natural 'data detective'. When the business requires data from unfamiliar or undocumented upstream systems, you will proactively hunt down the external business owners, ask the right investigative questions to decode their data structures, and document the requirements. You will build temporary technical workarounds in our Snowflake environment to keep the business agile, while carefully documenting the underlying technical gaps so they can be prioritized for permanent, long-term BT automation.
 Responsibilities 
 Gold & Reporting Layer Development: Actively develop, model, and optimize highly aggregated datasets, schemas, and tables in GIC's Snowflake Gold and Reporting layers. Transform cleaned, raw data sources into production-ready semantic models designed specifically to fuel BI tools and handle complex, high-priority ad-hoc business requests.
 Requirements Translation & Technical Discovery: Partner with business analysts in Reporting and Decision Analytics to run upfront discovery on new requests. Dissect vague requests, clarify and document clear business logic, and verify data feasibility in Snowflake before starting SQL development.

We are building a platform to model and manage the flow of information within healthcare organisations, improving outcomes for patients, payers, and healthcare providers. We believe data handling in current healthcare systems is needlessly complex and disconnected, leading to isolated and inefficient decision making. To showcase how this technology can advance the delivery of healthcare and improve lives, we build and deploy products for healthcare providers and payers into the UK and US markets.
Dyad is a fast-growing, Series A-funded health tech company with a team of more than 70 people. We are expanding quickly as we grow from primary care into NHS secondary care and new international markets. We are passionate about technology and its applications in worthwhile ventures. New joiners will have a significant impact on the direction of the company, as well as our culture.
 Our products 
 Dyad's Platform : Dyad's products are founded upon our Semantic AI platform, which enables payers and providers to access cutting-edge AI capabilities for their own use cases and applications. Our partners either use the platform APIs directly or work with us to develop applications for their use cases. 
 BetterLetter , our AI tool helping practices decrease their admin burden in processing clinical letters. We use this to reduce staff time spent identifying codes to be applied to the record as well as suggesting follow-up tasks and workflow optimisations. BetterLetter helps providers save time, save cost, improve performance under audit and build staffing resilience.
 The role 
As Operations Manager at Dyad, you will make sure the company runs smoothly as we grow. You will own our London office and workplace, and act as the right hand of our VP Business Operations across purchasing, supplier management, people operations logistics and IT administration.

You will help make sure our operations are both efficient and audit-ready.
We want someone who has run operations before, anticipates problems before they land, and is comfortable owning a function rather than working through a task list. You will be the person who makes sure new starters have a great first day, suppliers get paid on time, the office works, and leavers are offboarded cleanly and securely.

 Core responsibilities 
 Office and workplace Own the day-to-day running of the office, including supplies, maintenance, health and safety, and the working environment. Be the first point of contact for internal and external office queries.
 Building and physical security Manage relationships with building management, the landlord and other tenants. Look after building access, visitor management and the security of restricted areas such as our IT room, as part of our ISO 27001 physical security controls.
 Events Plan and run on-site events, team days and visitor logistics.
 Joiners, movers and leavers Run the practical side of onboarding and offboarding: equipment, desks, building access, first-day experience and exit logistics. Work with our HR Manager, who owns contracts, onboarding and probation in Personio, and our IT Operations Analyst, who manages system access, so every leaver's access and equipment is recovered on their last day.
 People operations support Support the HR Manager with employee records, payro
[...]
ackstop Act as backup for the VP Business Operations, keeping things moving when they are away or at capacity, within agreed decision-making and spending limits. Take on ad hoc projects as priorities change.
 Requirements

3 to 5 years' experience in an operations management role, ideally in a startup or fast-growing business.
A track record of owning office and facilities management, not just supporting it.
Hands-on experience of onboarding and offboarding, HR administration and purchasing.
Confidence with everyday finance processes such as invoicing, expenses and supplier payments.
Strong Google Workspace skills and confidence learning new HR, finance and IT admin platforms.
Excellent organisation and communication skills and the confidence to deal with senior colleagues and suppliers.

Experience supporting ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus, DSPT or similar compliance work.

This is a backfill role within Lansweeper's Revenue Operations team, built for someone who wants to spend meaningful time designing and building AI agents — not just maintaining systems. As a GTM Applications Engineer (AI Agents & Integrations), you'll own the technical layer connecting our go-to-market application stack while actively identifying where AI can eliminate admin overhead, consolidate tooling, and automate GTM processes end-to-end. In this version of the role, you won't wait to be told where AI fits — you'll proactively find it, prototype it, and build it. The stack is your canvas; agents and skills are how you leave your mark.
 Challenge: 
The main challenges you'll face are:
 Breadth across platforms — the GTM stack spans Gainsight, Gong, ZoomInfo, ZoomPhone, DocuSign, Salesforce, and more. You'll need to stay technically sharp and agile across all of them, adapting quickly as each platform evolves.
 Agentic work at the frontier . Building and orchestrating AI agents, whether in Workato, LangChain, Claude managed agents, or Salesforce Agentforce, is still emerging practice. You'll be working without a full playbook, which requires comfort with ambiguity and a bias for experimentation.
 Self-directed identification of AI opportunities — rather than waiting for direction, you'll be expected to surface process gaps, evaluate their AI-fit, and propose solutions. That requires both technical fluency and strong GTM process understanding.

Own configuration, administration, and troubleshooting for the GTM application stack.
Build and maintain integrations and data pipelines between GTM applications and Salesforce (e.g., Snowflake to Gainsight).
Proactively identify GTM process areas where AI agents, automation, or AI-assisted workflows can reduce admin burden, consolidate tooling, or improve data quality.
Design, build, and deploy AI agents across the stack, using whichever platform fits the job (Workato, LangChain, Claude managed agents, Salesforce Agentforce, or equivalent), from scoping and prompt engineering through orchestration and into production.
Monitor observability for deployed agents. Track what they do in production, catch failures or drift early, and iterate based on real usage.
Build human-in-the-loop checkpoints for agentic workflows. Decide where an agent should escalate to a person instead of acting on its own, and design that approval or fallback path.
Provide technical guidance and drive improvements across GTM systems projects, becoming the senior technical voice for AI integration within the stack.
Take on lighter Salesforce administration and configuration tasks (fields, flows, permissions) alongside the Salesforce team.
Evaluate and onboard new AI tools and GTM applications as the stack evolves, staying ahead of what's available and what's production-ready.
Partner with GTM Ops, Sales, and Customer Success stakeholders to translate process needs into scalable, AI-augmented technical solutions.

2–4 years in a technical applications, systems administration, or integrations role within Corporate environments
Hands-on experience building with AI agents or AI-assisted tooling — production deployments, internal pilots, or substantive personal projects.
Practical prompt engineering skills — able to design, test, and iterate prompts within AI platforms to produce reliable, production-grade outputs.

Lead a team of analytical and operational business partners that are aligned to the CS organization
Drive the operating rhythm of our business including monthly and quarterly business reviews, forecasting, org deep dives, and ongoing business planning efforts (including contributing to headcount and capacity planning, account and territory assignments, etc.)
Partner with Senior CS and Operations leadership to drive market and segment-specific analyses to uncover insight, influence key decisions, and shape the longer-term vision of the team

Derive understanding and insights on emerging trends from our data and present recommendations on how we can drive better outcomes to CS leadership
Influence the data and systems strategy and processes required to scale commercial teams

Conceptualize and pilot new programs to test the effectiveness of various CS workflows, structures, and decisions
Collaborate with various business units to drive productivity and headcount scenario analyses

Bachelor’s Degree with a quantitative focus (Economics, Finance, Computer Science, Mathematics, etc.)
5+ years of work experience in either CS, Sales, GTM Strategy and/or Operations
1+ years of leadership experience
Comfortable being in a player-coach manager type role
Familiarity with consumption-based software business models
Experience as a business partner to a field organization
Experience with at least one major business intelligence tool (Tableau, Google Data Studio, Looker)
The Ideal Candidate
Thrives in working in a fast-paced working environment
Effective communicator who can break down convoluted technical, financial, or operational concepts into simple business vernacular

You’re intensely curious. You want to know how things work, and you want to know why, and you’re comfortable getting your hands dirty in data and process to get there

BoodleBox is a VC-backed GenAI platform built for higher education. With 100,000+ users across 1,200+ colleges and universities, we partner with faculty, staff, and students to make responsible AI adoption practical, impactful, and lasting. Our platform brings together leading AI tools — including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity — under one roof, purpose-built for the unique demands of academic environments. We’re guided by three core values: service, education, and collaboration.

The Role
You’re the person a trial lawyer wants in the room when someone asks whether the AI can really do this. You run the demo, answer the security question nobody saw coming, and you’re still there three months later when the firm is using it without you. Law firms don’t buy AI on a pitch deck. They buy it when they see their own workflows, their own documents, and their own security requirements handled cleanly.
BoodleBox is the platform that powered Mark Lanier’s trial team, turning partner expertise into 200+ custom bots and courtroom-grade AI workflows into something other firms can adopt. We now work with 46 law firms, and law firm accounts have expanded 210%. After the Lanier Meta trial, revenue grew from about $100K a month to about $300K a month in 90 days. You’re the person who makes the next firm look like that.
You sit at the center of every Law deal, between sales, product, and the firms using BoodleBox to win cases. This role is fully remote, with a company hub in Colorado Springs, CO.

 Technical credibility in every Law deal. You run discovery and live demos for trial lawyers and firm IT and security teams, and every “can it do X” gets a confident answer.

 New firms going live. You own configuration, custom bot setup, and training for partners and staff, and you decide when an account is ready.
 Adoption beyond the first champion. You run firm-wide rollout and usage reviews until one believer becomes the whole firm’s habit.
 Expansion signals that reach the right people. More seats, more practice groups, more services: you spot them and hand qualified signals to Legal GTM.
 The voice of the firm in product. Connector requests and feature gaps go from the firms to Product and Engineering with your fingerprints on the priority.
 The Law playbook. Demo scripts, security FAQs, and onboarding checklists are yours, and you keep them current so the next firm goes faster than the last.

 You’ve turned a skeptic into a champion. You can name the room, the objection, and the moment it changed.

 Customer Success Manager – EcoPlant 
 Location: Remote – Continental United States
 About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.
EcoPlant combines software as a service (SaaS), industrial Internet of Things (IoT) technology, and predictive analytics to monitor, control, and optimize compressed-air systems. Its platform helps customers improve energy efficiency and reliability while understanding system performance, operating costs, and savings.
 Job Overview: 
The Customer Success Manager serves as a key point of contact for EcoPlant customers and channel partners, helping them understand and recognize value from the platform. Beginning after system installation, this role leads customer onboarding, provides dashboard training, and coordinates ongoing support. Working closely with account managers, Technical Support, Engineering, and Product teams, the Customer Success Manager translates system data into clear insights, supports business reviews and renewal discussions, and helps improve the overall customer experience.
 Responsibilities: 
Lead customer onboarding following system installation, helping users understand the EcoPlant dashboard, system information, and platform capabilities.
Build and maintain relationships with customers and channel partners, serving as an ongoing contact for platform questions, training, and support needs.
Provide training to customer contacts and new users, supporting continued platform adoption as customer personnel, equipment, or requirements change.
Review platform data to help customers understand compressed-air system performance, energy consumption, operating costs, and savings.
Identify system performance concerns and improvement opportunities, partnering with technical resources to evaluate findings and coordinate appropriate actions.
Prepare and deliver quarterly or annual business reviews, as needed, to communicate customer value and align on financial, operational, and sustainability goals.
Support account managers and channel partners with renewal and expansion conversations by preparing performance highlights, customer value summaries, and supporting information.
Coordinate with Technical Support, Engineering, Operations, and R&D to address customer concerns and follow issues through resolution.
Document customer feedback and submit product enhancement requests to Product and R&D teams, including colleagues in Israel.
Establish repeatable onboarding, training, communication, and customer success practices, and support customer case studies and performance documentation.
 Requirements: 
High school diploma or GED
[...]
 within the continental United States. Candidates should have access to a major airport for business travel. Travel up to 30% across North America may be required, although actual travel is expected to be infrequent and based on customer and business needs, including customer meetings and system performance reviews.
 Pay Range: 
 The total pay range for this role, including incentives, is $90,000–$145,000 . The actual pay range takes into acco
[...]
raining; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.
 What We Offer 
 At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment — as well as for our individual well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support needed to take charge of your health and future.
Our benefits include healthcare coverage (medical, prescription, dental, and vision), wellness programs, life insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off, and an employee stock program, among other offerings. These benefits, combined with our pay transparency and inclusive culture, reflect our commitment to supporting you at work and beyond.
Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency.

PagerDuty, Inc. (NYSE: PD) is the global leader in AI-first digital operations. By automatically detecting, diagnosing, and remediating issues, the PagerDuty Platform orchestrates AI agents and automated workflows with context from over 750 integrations. Trusted by approximately two-thirds of the Fortune 100 and nearly half of the Fortune 500, PagerDuty is the industry standard for organizations scaling resilient, autonomous operations. Notable customers include Chipotle, Cloudflare, Docusign, Fox, Nvidia, Salesforce, Spotify, Zoom and more. We are growing rapidly and hiring top talent with leading AI skills across engineering, sales, product, marketing, and beyond as we build the leading digital operations platform.
 About the role 
As a Senior Principal Customer Success Manager you will be an executive-facing partner to some of PagerDuty’s most important enterprise customers across the UK, Ireland and wider EMEA. You will build value relationships with the leaders who own incident response and reliability, and shape how their organisations use PagerDuty to meet their goals. You will work closely with Sales, Product and Marketing, and you will share what you build so the whole team gets better.
 What you’ll do 
Own the customer journey end to end, from strategic kick-off and the Sales handover through to QBRs, renewal and expansion, and hold the standard consistent across your accounts.
Build value relationships with the executives accountable for incident management, alerting and service reliability, not only the teams who use the product day to day.
Co-create a strategic roadmap with each customer, aligned to their critical OKRs for incident response and alerting, and agree objectives and measures with them.
Lead the change that comes with it: process, ownership and behaviour, so customers adopt what they have bought and keep using it.
Run executive business reviews that set direction for the next period, not only report on the last one.
Identify risks to customer goals early, agree mitigation with the customer and Sales, and own the outcome.
Work across Sales, Product and Marketing to grow accounts, feed customer evidence into the roadmap, and sharpen how we position value.
Advise customers on best practice across incident and alerting workflows, and build playbooks, AI agents and shared assets that help both customers and the CS team.
 Basic Qualifications: 
Six to ten years in enterprise Customer Success, account management or a similar role, with sustained engagement at VP and C-level.
A track record of taking customers from little use to full use, and of renewal and expansion outcomes you can show.
Experience building value cases and running reviews that change decisions.
A working understanding of incident management, alerting and DevOps, enough to advise practitioners on integrations and workflows.
Daily, hands-on use of AI tools such as Claude or OpenAI Codex, and a record of building something others now use, whether for customers or your team.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
Fluency in German or French.
Experience moving customers to consumption, credit or AI-based pricing.
Examples of AI skills or workflows you built for your team, and how they changed the way it works.
There will be some customer travel within Europe required for this role and be working out of our brand new designed London office 2 days a week.
 Hesitant to apply? 
We encourage you to submit your resume even if you don't meet every requirement. We value potential and consider each candidate's full professional story. Whether you're exploring a career change or taking your next step, we look forward to reviewing your application. If this just isn’t the right role or time - sign up for job alerts !
 Where we work 
PagerDuty operates a hybrid work model with offices in 8 major cities: Atlanta, Lisbon, London, San Francisco, Santiago, Sydney, Tokyo, and Toronto. While we offer flexibility within our established locations, we cannot employ candidates residing in:

Job title: Sales Operations Associate 
 Location: Remote (U.S.) — Utah preferred 
 Type: Full-time 
 Compensation: $ 85,000–$100,000 base salary (DOE) plus a target annual bonus of 15%. Total target compensation ranges from approximately $98,000–$115,000+, based on experience and performance. 
 About Avari 
 Avari is a fast-growing short-term rental property management company, operating in partnership with Casago across Florida's Gulf Coast, Alabama, Utah, Nevada, Oregon, and the Lake Tahoe region of California. As we continue to expand through strategic acquisitions and new market growth, we help homeowners maximize the value of their vacation rental investments through exceptional management and proven returns. This role plays a key part in strengthening our market expansion, sales outreach, and revenue operations as we scale nationwide.
 About the role 
As a Sales Operations Associate with Avari Management, this role sits at the intersection of data and the field. You'll mine market-level data to surface homeowner-acquisition opportunities in our priority markets, translate those insights into clear messaging and collateral for our reps, and provide the sales operations backbone — quota tracking, payouts, and forecasting support — that keeps the team running.
In short: you turn "here's what the data says" into "here's exactly what our reps should say and send," and you keep the numbers behind the sales team honest and current. You're happiest with a lot of surface area, moving fast, and a mix of analysis, communication, and operations in a single week.v
 What you'll do 
 Market intelligence & analysis 
Mine internal and third-party data (CRM, data warehouse, STR market data, property/ownership records) to identify high-opportunity markets, owner segments, and competitive dynamics.
Build repeatable market profiles covering owner density, competitor presence, pricing, seasonality, and regulatory considerations.
Partner with RevOps on enrichment workflows so the data feeding the field stays accurate and current.
 Messaging & collateral 
Translate market insights into clear value propositions tailored by market and owner segment.
Create rep-ready collateral: one-pagers, outreach/email templates, call scripts, market briefs, and objection-handling guides.
Keep the content library organized so reps can find and use what they need.
 Sales enablement & adoption 
Equip BD/sales reps with the market playbooks, messaging, and collateral they need to win owners in each region.
Onboard and train reps on positioning, tooling, and plays, and drive real adoption — not just published assets.
Run feedback loops with reps to learn what's landing in-market and refine accordingly.
 Sales operations support 
Track quota attainment across the sales team and calculate commission/payouts accurately and on time.
Support forecasting and pipeline reporting, including operating the team's pipeline-weighting and projected-revenue reporting.
Maintain CRM hygiene and build reporting that connects rep activity and enablement to pipeline and owner signings.
 What you'll bring 
 Required 
3–4 years in sales/revenue operations, sales enablement, analytics, growth, or another data-forward GTM role.
 Strong with data — you pull, analyze, and interpret it without hand-holding. Fluent in spreadsheets and CRM, and quick to pick up SQL or BI tools.
 Tech-native — you learn new tools fast and instinctively look for ways to automate and streamline.
 Communicate insights well — you turn a dataset into a clear, persuasive narrative and into material a rep can actually use.
 High energy and pace — you thrive with lots of moving parts, ambiguity, and a fast tempo, and you take ownership without waiting to be told.
Comfort with numbers behind a sales team: quota, commissions/payouts, and forecasting mechanics (or a clear aptitude to ramp quickly).
 Preferred 
Experience in proptech, real estate, hospitality, marketplaces, franchise/multi-location, or other geographically segmented go-to-market models.
HubSpot and/or data-warehouse (e.g., Snowflake) experience.
Familiarity with prospecting/enrichment tooling (e.g., Clay) and STR or local-market data sources.
Exposure to owner-, SMB-, or B2B2C-acquisition motions.
 What success looks like 
 First 90 days: market profiles for the top [3–5] priority markets, a first rep-facing playbook in market, and clean, reliable quota/attainment reporting the team trusts.
 First 6–12 months: measurable rep adoption of collateral, demonstrable conversion lift in enabled markets, and a repeatable "market → messaging → enablement" motion — with sales ops reporting running like clockwork.
 Compensation & benefits 
Base salary range: $85,000 – $100,000, depending on experience.
Performance bonus: 15% target annual bonus (bringing target total compensation to approximately $98,000–$115,000+, depending on base salary and performance).
Health, dental, vision, 401(k) match, unlimited PTO & remote-first culture.
Professional development and career growth opportunities

Customer Success Manager 
 Remote 
 Employment Type: Full-Time 
 About Nsight Health 
 Nsight Health is transforming how care is delivered through Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM), Chronic Care Management (CCM), and Behavioral Health Integration (BHI). We empower healthcare providers to manage chronic conditions using real-time data, AI-enabled technology, and 24/7 clinical support. Our HIPAA-compliant platform connects patients and care teams nationwide—improving outcomes, adherence, and peace of mind. Join a fast-growing, mission-driven team that blends healthcare and technology to make a measurable difference in people’s lives. 
 Nsight Health — Where Technology Meets Compassion. 
 Position Summary 
 We are seeking a Customer Success Manager to own the health and retention of a portfolio of provider accounts. Reporting to the Director of Customer Success, you are the senior point of contact above the front line — the person providers trust with their hardest questions and the one who keeps their program delivering value month over month. 
 You own account health, drive retention, move accounts onto durable long-term agreements, and project manage complex issues to clean resolution. You partner with the Customer Growth team in a shared pod model to keep your accounts both healthy and expanding, and you bring clinical value to the foreground — surfacing outcomes, care gaps, and trends that show providers exactly what the program is doing for their patients. 
 Our clients are sophisticated physicians, and you meet them with equal credibility. You engage escalations directly, de-escalate with composure, and turn pressure into a stronger relationship. This is a role for someone who takes real ownership of their book, fights for every account, and is energized by keeping it healthy as the company grows. 
 AI Fluency Requirement - Non-Negotiable 
 Nsight Health is an AI-first organization. Every member of our leadership and operations team is expected to actively use AI tools in their day-to-day work - not as a novelty, but as a core productivity multiplier. This role requires genuine curiosity about AI, comfort experimenting with tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and workflow automation platforms, and the judgment to know when AI helps and when it doesn't. If AI makes you uncomfortable, this is not the right role. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Account Health and Retention : Own the health and status of your assigned accounts against a clear green, yellow, and red standard, keeping a direct line to each decision maker so every account can be championed when it counts. Own retention on your accounts, surfacing risk early and pulling in your Director, Support, Implementation, and Customer Growth partners to keep at-risk accounts whole. Move your accounts onto durable long-term agreements that protect and compound the book. Own the warm handoff from Sales and Growth into Customer Success at go-live, confirming that what was sold is what gets delivered. 
 Issue Resolution and Service : Serve as the senior point of contact above the front line, engaging providers directly to resolve and de-escalate the hardest issues with composure. Project manage issues to resolution, coordinating Support and Implementation to close them cleanly and keep the provider informed throughout. Action non-adherent patients and bring proactive clinical value to your providers, using care gaps, outcome trending, and program reporting to raise the value they see in the program. Run quarterly business reviews and provider reporting, keeping clinical results and program value in front of every account you own. 
 Cadence and Collaboration : Participate in the Customer Success deep dive and escalation sync, the dedicated team session for working escalations and account detail. Partner in the pod model with Customer Growth, using the healthy tension between retention and growth to keep your accounts both well and expanding. Stay tightly aligned with the Implementation and Support teams so that handoffs are clean and issues resolve quickly. 
 Data and Continuous Improvement : Maintain accurate account health, status, and activity in HubSpot so that your book reads clear
[...]
del alongside a growth or sales team. 
 Compensation & Benefits 
 Competitive base pay: $110,000 – $135,000 annually. 
 Additional Compensation: 
 Performance-Based Bonus: Eligible for an annual bonus based on company and individual performance. 
 Benefits Include: 
 PTO Accrual 
 Medical, Dental, Vision, and supplemental insurance options 
 401(k) Plan with 3.5% Company Match 
 Company-provided equipment 
 Join Our Mission-Driven Team 
 At Nsight Health, you will be part of a fast-growing organization at the intersection of healthcare, technology, and compassion. We are looking for a Customer Success Manager who takes real ownership of their book, shows up with clinical credibility and commercial instinct, and is energized by the challenge of keeping sophisticated provider relationships healthy, growing, and built to last.

About us: 
Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets through automating and streamlining the work of assurance and audit practitioners specifically within cybersecurity, privacy, and ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance). Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.
We’re based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, DNX Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Justin Kan, Eric Ries, and more.
We value diversity — in backgrounds and in experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide’s team is inclusive, driven, humble and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture that we are building, seeking teammates that are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.
As an early-stage start-up employee, you’ll have the opportunity to build out the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners’ lives easier by eliminating up to 50% of their work and giving them better work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you will find a home at Fieldguide.
 About the role: 
Fieldguide is seeking a Sales Enablement Manager to join our growing sales enablement team. As our dedicated enablement lead for Corporate Internal Audit (IA) and Public Sector, you'll play a crucial role in shaping and elevating the performance of the sellers who cover these segments. This position offers a unique opportunity to build and implement segment-specific enablement strategies from the ground up, directly impacting Fieldguide's growth trajectory as we expand beyond CPA and advisory firms into corporate audit functions and government buyers.
In this role, you'll be the driving force behind our sales team's success in these markets, creating and delivering targeted training programs, developing critical sales content, and serving as a trusted advisor to our Account Executives. Your expertise in sales methodologies and in how corporate and public sector organizations buy will be instrumental in optimizing our sales processes and enhancing our team's effectiveness in a competitive market.
 What you'll do: 
Enhance our current sales enablement programs, including new hire onboarding and ongoing training initiatives, with dedicated tracks for Corporate IA and Public Sector
Develop and deliver content for sales training, covering industry knowledge, product expertise, and sales methodologies, including internal audit frameworks and standards and public sector compliance frameworks
Serve as the company's expert on sales methodology (MEDDPICC), ensuring effective implementation across the sales organization
Develop Public Sector buying-process enablement: RFP/RFI/RFQ response, fiscal-year and budget-cycle timing, procurement vehicles and other relevant requirements
Build Corporate IA buyer enablement
Conduct regular 1:1 sessions with Account Executives, providing personalized coaching grounded in real call review and driving adoption of best practices
Collaborate closely with marketing to align sales enablement efforts with broader company messaging and initiatives, including events and associations relevant to these segments
Analyze team performance metrics by segment to identify areas for improvement and develop targeted enablement strategies
Stay current on industry trends, regulatory changes, government budget cycles, and competitors to inform and enhance our sales approach
 About you: 
5-7+ years of experience in sales enablement in a B2B SaaS environment, preferably vertical SaaS, with direct experience enabling teams that sell to enterprise and/or public sector buyers
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Business, Marketing, or a related field, or equivalent work experience
Deep expertise in sales methodologies, particularly MEDDPICC/MEDDIC, and applying them to complex, multi-stakeholder deals
Strong technical aptitude with the ability to quickly grasp and articulate complex product features
Demonstrated success in onboarding and ramping up new sales hires
Self-starter mentality with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving startup environment
Data-driven approach to measuring the impact of enablement initiatives
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships across all levels of the organization
Flexibility to adapt to changing priorities and take on additional responsibilities as needed
 Bonus points if you have: 
Experience as a practitioner in audit/advisory, ideally in a corporate internal audit function (CIA, CPA, or CISA a plus)
Working knowledge of internal audit, SOX, and enterprise risk, and/or public sector procurement and compliance frameworks
Experience selling to or working in government (federal, state, local, or education), including RFP and procurement processes
 More about Fieldguide: 
Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are:
Fearless - Inspire & break down seemingly impossible walls.
Fast - Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection.
Lovable - ​​Deliver happiness & 11 star experiences.
Owners - Execute & run the business with ownership.
Win-win - Create mutual value & earn trust for life.
Inclusive - Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams.
 Some of our benefits include: 
Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership
Unlimited PTO
401k
Wellness benefits, including a bundle of free therapy sessions
Technology & Work from Home reimbursement
Flexible work schedules

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 
We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

Revenue Strategy & Operations is the team behind how Horizon3's go-to-market organization is planned, run and measured. We own budgeting and headcount planning, quota and compensation, territory planning and management (accounts, opportunities, leads and routing), goals for pipeline and performance, forecasting, performance management, and the operating process the sales organization runs on. Regional partners carry that scope for their sales leaders in AMER, EMEA and APJ. Global Centers of Excellence set the standards they all run on. This role is the Core Operations center of excellence: the operating process, the territory and change management standards, and the data the whole organization runs on.

The goal is one standard across every region, with systems that match what the field is actually doing.
You will work with Sales leadership, the regional Revenue Strategy & Operations partners and GTM Systems. The regional partners own the relationship with each sales leader. GTM Systems builds and runs the tools. You own the process in between, and you make sure it gets done.

hc-ashby___keebler-health___c9c83ec2-502.description:
About the Role 
Keebler Health is building the operating system for value-based care. Our mission is to help risk-bearing healthcare organizations thrive in value-based arrangements by unlocking the full power of their data. We empower leading primary care groups, ACOs, and health plans to act on real-time insights that improve outcomes, reduce costs, and fuel sustainable growth.
We are looking for a Customer Success Manager to be the face of Keebler Health for our customers. You will own the relationship, act as the customer’s advocate inside our company, and make sure they see real value from the platform and want to grow with us. You will work closely with our Implementation team, who own the technical build, while you stay the person the customer knows and trusts from the late stages of the sale through go-live and the long-term partnership that follows.
This is a US-based remote position. We have a strong preference for candidates based in North Carolina or New York, where our team hubs are.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Customer Relationships 
Own the relationship for your portfolio of accounts, from late-stage sales through onboarding and ongoing partnership.
Join late-stage sales conversations to help set realistic expectations before contract signature.
Build trusted relationships with executive, clinical, operational, and technical stakeholders, and keep building them as people and priorities change.
Be the customer’s advocate inside Keebler Health, making sure their needs, feedback, and concerns reach Product, Engineering, and Clinical teams and get answered.
Understand each customer’s goals, challenges, and measures of success, and tell their story clearly to our internal teams.
Develop account plans, stakeholder maps, and communication rhythms for each account.
Lead regular business reviews, executive check-ins, and planning conversations.
Be a key part of renewals, and help customers get the most from their relationship with us by identifying additional features and opportunities that fit their goals.
Monitor account health and address risks, gaps, and opportunities before the customer has to raise them.
 Managing a Portfolio 
Balance competing priorities across several customers, deciding where your time and our team’s time will have the most impact.
Manage requests, issues, and escalations through to resolution, coordinating with Implementation, Support, Product, Engineering, and Clinical teams.
Set honest expectations with customers about timing and scope, and say no or not yet when you need to.
Keep commitments visible so that important details do not fall through the cracks.
Hold stakeholders, internal and external, accountable while maintaining strong working relationships.
 Working with Implementation 
Partner with the Implementation team through onboarding so the handoff to ongoing account management is smooth and nothing is lost.
Drive adoption across practices and user groups, including bringing on new users and sites over time.
Share structured customer feedback and contribute to repeatable customer success processes and playbooks.
 What Success Looks Like 
We're moving fast as a company, and things will change rapidly, but below is a sense of what success could look like in this role:
First 30 days: learn our platform, customers, and internal teams, and meet the stakeholders for your accounts as well as take ownership of steady state customers.
First 90 days: own your account portfolio, with account plans in place and your first quarterly business reviews completed.
First year: customers who are live and using the platform, clear measures of value, and renewals or expansions that reflect it.
 About You 
 Your Experience 
3-5+ years in customer success, account management, or another customer-facing role, ideally in software.
A track record of owning customer relationships and growing or renewing accounts, with measurable results.
Sales skills: you are comfortable running a commercial conversation, spotting an opening, and asking for the next step.
Credibility with senior customers and the confidence to have difficult conversations.
Strong organization and the ability to juggle competing priorities across several accounts without dropping the ball.
Ability to work with technical and non-technical teams without direct authority.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Comfortable working in an early-stage or rapidly changing environment.
Value-based care or healthcare technology experience is a nice to have, not a requirement. If you’re strong in the rest and curious about the industry, we want to hear from you.
 How You Work 
Takes ownership of outcomes and drives them forward independently.
Combines real empathy for the customer with operational discipline.
Stays calm and clear under pressure, including when a customer is unhappy.
Advocates for customers without losing sight of what is realistic for Keebler Health.
Communicates credibly with everyone from a clinician inside a practice to an executive inside a parent organization.
Motivated by compounding results, where the second year of an account is stronger because of how the first year was run.
Uses LLMs and AI tools to remove friction and build capacity, and improves the team’s systems alongside their own output.
 What We Offer 
Competitive salary, equity options, and benefits package.
A fast-paced, innovative environment.
Professional growth and development opportunities.
A collaborative and supportive team culture.
The chance to shape a foundational role and make a meaningful impact on the healthcare industry.

Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We're trusted by 20,000 organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide.
Our customers (researchers, marketers, HR teams, nonprofits, and platform businesses) rave about how fast and easy Tremendous is to use. Check out our ratings on G2 .
Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. We're a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life. The team agrees– our employee NPS is in the high 80s.
 About the role 
We’re hiring a Senior Customer Success Manager to onboard, retain, and grow high-value international clients. You’ll be the primary CSM for EMEA and Indian clients, with selected accounts in other Asian markets where working hours align. You’ll own those relationships from late-stage sales through implementation and ongoing growth.
You’ll join our Customer Success team, with day-to-day support from your manager and the broader Success team. You’ll also work closely with the International team, joining relevant meetings and getting help with questions and escalations outside US working hours.
 What you'll do 
Lead onboarding and launch planning for high-value clients.
Own a portfolio of enterprise and mid-market relationships.
Run recurring meetings and monitor account health.
Retain business and find expansion opportunities.
Coordinate complex needs across Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Support, and Operations.
Run proactive calls during agreed working hours for clients in EMEA, India, and other assigned markets.
Improve and document our international Customer Success processes.
 What you'll bring 
4+ years in Customer Success, Account Management, or a related role
Experience managing enterprise or high-value B2B customers
A record of leading complex onboarding and implementation work
Strong commercial judgment and communication skills
Excellent English and residence on the US East Coast, in the UK, or in Spain
A sustainable commitment to 6am–2pm ET if based in the US. In the UK or Spain, availability for normal or later local business hours with regular US team overlap; we’ll agree on the exact schedule during hiring.
The ability to manage complex client relationships independently in a remote environment
German, French, or Spanish fluency is a plus.
Experience with SaaS, fintech, APIs, or payments is also helpful.
 You’ll thrive here if you 
Own outcomes without waiting for direction.
Keep complex implementations organized.
Stay calm and credible in difficult situations.
Balance customer needs with commercial judgment.
Enjoy building processes other people can use.
 What's cool about the role 
 Competitive pay and equity. Base salary for this role:
US: $160k to $240k.
UK: £100k - £150k
Spain: €85k - €140k
 Fully remote. Work from anywhere in Spain, the UK, or EST United States.
 Great culture. Read more about how we work in our public handbook .

Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We're trusted by 20,000 organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide.
Our customers (researchers, marketers, HR teams, nonprofits, and platform businesses) rave about how fast and easy Tremendous is to use. Check out our ratings on G2 .
Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. We’re a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life. The team agrees– our employee NPS is in the high 80s.
 What you'll do 
Serve as a high-leverage, cross-functional GTM utility player, taking ownership of a rotating set of high-priority initiatives. This could include:
Leading new-vertical exploration and driving the first wave of GTM execution.
Owning competitive intelligence across priority use cases and industries.
Identifying, investigating, and validating new growth levers and emerging trends.
Producing sharp, actionable analyses in days—not weeks.
Developing credible market sizing estimates in weeks—not months.

Being an operator at a start-up
Strong written communication skills. We’re a documentation-first culture.
